event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. TLDR: If tmux's process-title handling replaces its original argument vector, startup's new verification could refuse to end the legacy server; existing processes could remain behind the interrupted rows. Source basis: names_tmux_server_socket requires literal consecutive -S and socket arguments (process.rs:181-183), passed by old_terminals.rs:225-230, and refusal leaves the server alone (old_terminals.rs:260-265). The patch's unit test checks manufactured argument vectors only. Checked: complete assigned process patch, verification implementation, caller, and pinned Terminal substrate contract; those assert original arguments remain but do not themselves establish tmux's upstream behavior. Exact missing premise: argv as returned by the existing platform process reader for supported tmux servers after process-title setup. Next check: platform argv reader, server startup command, and primary tmux source. Suggested bucket: other pending route; potentially high if common inability to retire legacy agents; could-be-highest requires an established additional harm route, not yet shown. Confidence: uninvestigated lead, not a finding; no execution. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none.

event.summary: tmux process-title setup does not erase Linux socket argv
event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. TLDR considered: original concern was failure to retire legacy servers, leaving agents behind interrupted rows if process-title setup erased -S/socket arguments. Source investigation refutes this route for the ordinary supported build: procs.rs:1123-1144 reads Linux /proc/pid/cmdline, while upstream tmux 3.7c server.c:187 calls proc_start and proc.c:183 calls setproctitle. Its compat/setproctitle.c:23-44 implements this with PR_SET_NAME only, which changes the process name without replacing argv; its other-platform fallback at 45-50 does nothing. configure.ac:160-184 uses this compatibility implementation when the platform has no setproctitle. Primary sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tmux/tmux/3.7c/server.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tmux/tmux/3.7c/proc.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tmux/tmux/3.7c/compat/setproctitle.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tmux/tmux/3.7c/configure.ac . Suggested bucket: other for the refuted verification concern; original potentially high consequence preserved above. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss route; concurrent-agent harm was only a possible additional premise, and startup failure policy explicitly accepts a second agent. Confidence: source-supported refutation, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation, not merely specification acceptance. possible_cover: none. Caveat: a deliberately custom-linked tmux with different process-title implementation was not established as an ordinary supported configuration; no claim of runtime verification or of argv inspection on every packaged tmux variant.

event.summary: Checked tmux platform implementations preserve socket argv
event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. Synthesis expands the earlier Linux-only check. Original TLDR/consequence preserved: if process-title setup erased the original -S/socket pair, verification would leave a legacy server/agents behind interrupted rows, potentially a material UX failure. Suggested bucket other for a source-refuted concern, original potentially high consequence retained; could-be-highest: no established further loss/security route for this concern. Confidence: source-supported refutation for the inspected ordinary platform build paths, no execution. Checks/results: pinned .github/release/source-pins.env names tmux 3.7c. scripts/build-private-tmux.sh:73-74 downloads the checksum-pinned upstream release; 94-133 selects musl Linux or aarch64 Darwin and 155-167 configures it without a process-title patch or libbsd injection. Upstream tmux 3.7c and 3.8 compat/setproctitle.c:23-44 use PR_SET_NAME on Linux (glibc or musl), which changes the comm name, not argv; 45-50 is a no-op on the Darwin fallback. configure.ac selects this compatibility implementation when no native setproctitle exists. The currently fetched Homebrew formula uses unpatched upstream tmux 3.8 and does not add libbsd or a process-title patch. Apple's libc _stdlib.h exposes getprogname/setprogname but no setproctitle; together with the upstream fallback this supports the ordinary Homebrew/Darwin inference, not an observation of a running Mac. procs.rs:1721-1755 and parse_procargs2_argv:794-839 read the Darwin argv region, not the process comm name or environment; Linux reads /proc/pid/cmdline. An older upstream 3.2a source check also showed the same PR_SET_NAME/no-op implementation, although that is below this revision's version floor. proposed_drop: source refutation of process-title-induced argv loss in the inspected supported build routes; not justified merely by the nonfatal retirement failure policy. Exact supported-build contract, SPEC.md:5276-5283: "The supported tmux is either the pinned build Farhelm itself installs or ships, or the stock tmux package of the platform's standard package source (the Linux distribution, or Homebrew on a Mac), at or above the version floor, run as the real binary." and "Anything else is unsupported, including wrapper scripts, custom or patched builds, and configuration or behavior a stock package would not bring." Primary sources checked this turn: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tmux/tmux/3.8/compat/setproctitle.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tmux/tmux/3.8/configure.ac ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/master/Formula/t/tmux.rb ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apple-oss-distributions/Libc/main/include/_stdlib.h . Prior event retains the 3.7c URLs. possible_cover: none known. Caveats: no claim that every distro's historic package binary was executed or every future package patch audited. No actual supported variant with argv replacement was identified; a concrete stock package doing so would reopen this ID. Current Homebrew source was checked as an additional supported variant, not misrepresented as the historical package installed on a reviewed user's machine.

event.summary: Unit-test host launcher deliberately supports glibc Linux only
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 70bc66a9f285cc2a9984924f389834d118b7cfdc. TLDR considered: unit tests that require a real host now fail on macOS or musl because their test binary has no host initializer. Details: hosts/test_program.rs:41-43 always returns the test binary, but its entry module is cfg(all(target_os = linux, target_env = gnu)) at 47; the initializer checks exactly the four expected arguments and forwards only --socket/path to terminal_host::main_entry (73-93). The real host launcher supplies exactly this argv and clears the child environment (hosts/spawn.rs:350-359). The separate exec before loader initialization precedes libtest's threads, satisfying terminal-host/src/spawn.rs:30-32's single-threaded contract. This does not put a fork in a test-runner worker. Suggested bucket: other, maintainer test portability. Could-be-highest: no. Confidence: confirmed source, no execution. proposed_drop: explicit specification acceptance. SPEC_impl.md at this commit lines 2311-2317, Turning terminal hosts on: "The supervisor crate's own unit tests have no `farhelm`, so their test binary is its own host program: started with a host's command line (`internal terminal-host --socket <path>`), a loader initializer in it runs the host crate's entry point before libtest's `main` starts any thread, and exits (`hosts::test_program`). It is registered on glibc Linux only; elsewhere every host start from a unit test is refused (libtest rejects the arguments), so those tests fail by name rather than run on another kind of terminal." possible_cover: none. Caveat: this disposition covers the explicit platform limitation and threading boundary, not every conceivable pre-main Rust initialization issue.
